---
title: "External data in the common space"
---

Several groups have built mouse brain datasets that are not IBL's: gene expression, cell-type
densities, connectivity, cortical depth. IBL has repackaged each of them into the atlas
reference space and ships them through this package.

That repackaging is the point of this page. These datasets are scattered across separate
how-tos and it is easy to miss that they are one family, built on one idea.

## Why a common space is worth the trouble

**The registration work is already done.** Each dataset has been put into the Allen reference
space once, carefully, by someone else. You are not aligning volumes.

**Each joins to your data by one key.** Either a coordinate or an Allen region id — nothing
more. If your recordings carry either, the join is a lookup.

**The existing tools keep working.** `remap`, the flat maps and the Swanson plot operate on any
per-region value. A connectivity weight and a firing rate are the same shape of thing to them,
so anything you can already plot for your own data, you can plot for these.

**Comparing modalities becomes a lookup in one atlas** rather than a registration project.

**Downloads are versioned** with their source release recorded.

Two limits belong in the same breath:

- The genomics grids are **coarse** — 200 µm, against the atlas's 10–50 µm — and MERFISH is
  interpolated between sections. These are not high-resolution volumes.
- The connectivity tables have **no grid at all**. They are region-level, so there is nothing
  to overlay on a slice directly.

## What is available

| Dataset | Joined by | Grid and axes |
|---|---|---|
| Allen Gene Expression Atlas | Voxel grid, Allen CCF labels downsampled from 25 µm | 200 µm, shape 58×41×67, axes (ML, DV, AP) |
| MERFISH volumes | The same 200 µm atlas object as gene expression | 200 µm, axes (ML, DV, AP) |
| MERFISH cells | Allen CCF coordinates converted to bregma-relative x, y, z | Continuous coordinates |
| Oh/Knox mesoscale connectivity | Allen structure ids and acronyms, 291 summary structures | No grid; region table |
| Harris cortico-thalamic hierarchy | Area acronyms, matching the connectivity table | No grid |
| Allen streamlines | Depth values on the ordinary atlas grid, Isocortex only | 10, 25 or 50 µm |

The gene expression volume is `(4345, 58, 41, 67)` — 4345 experiments by ML, DV, AP.

## Two things that will trip you up

**The genomics volumes break the axis convention.** They are built with `dims2xyz=[0, 2, 1]`
and ordered (ML, DV, AP), not the (AP, ML, DV) that
[Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd) teaches for the atlas volumes. Use the
atlas object the genomics module gives you rather than assuming the usual order.

**The two loaders disagree on their default.** `agea.load` returns the **raw** volume
(`label=''`). `merfish.load_volume` returns the **denoised** one — its default is
`label='processed'`, meaning NaNs filled, Gaussian-smoothed and renormalised. Pass `label=''`
to get the raw MERFISH volume. Note also that `load_volume` drops non-neuronal cell types
unless you pass `include_non_neuronal=True`.

If you are comparing the two modalities voxel by voxel, you are comparing a raw volume against
a smoothed one unless you say otherwise.

## Streamlines

The Allen streamlines are cortical depth values converted onto the ordinary atlas grid, at 10,
25 or 50 µm. They are **Isocortex only** — `xyz_to_depth` returns `nan` for coordinates
outside it, rather than raising, so check for NaNs rather than assuming a failure would be
loud.

They sit in this family because they are Allen data repackaged onto the standard grid, like
the others.

## Two source gaps

**The MERFISH publication is not named.** The code attributes the data to the Zhuang lab and
an Allen release, but cites no paper. If you publish using it, track down the citation
yourself.

**How the gene expression volumes were registered to the CCF is not recorded.** The scraping
scripts that built them do not state the method.
:::

## Coming: the lipid atlas

A lipid atlas is expected to join this family. It is not yet merged into the package, so there
is nothing to load and nothing documented here yet — this is a placeholder so you know it is
on the way.
